title: Rule of the Congregation (1QSa) — Hobah Research Reading
about: The Rule of the Congregation (1QSa), once copied together with the Community Rule, describes the congregation of Israel in the latter days. Its two columns address education, admission to communal responsibilities, rank, physical qualifications for certain offices, council procedure, and a future sacred meal at which the priest and the Messiah of Israel are present.

translation.status: Hobah provisional research reading — not a diplomatic line-by-line translation of 1QSa
translation.base_text: The ancient Hebrew 1QSa manuscript provides the source framework. The present English is a Hobah reader rendering of the substantially preserved sense of its two columns rather than a diplomatic transcription.
translation.method: New Hobah English prose follows the major recoverable sense of 1QSa without copying a modern copyrighted English translation. Damaged wording is acknowledged rather than presented with unwarranted certainty. A future direct edition must be checked line by line against a documented Hebrew transcription and identify restorations explicitly.
translation.confidence: Medium-high for the broad sense; not yet rated for exact line-level equivalence in broken or disputed lines
translation.notes: The messianic meal material preserves priestly precedence before the Messiah of Israel in this witness. The wording is not harmonized to later Christian or Jewish expectations. Reader labels replace a claim that the present English reproduces every line of each column exactly.
translation.license_note: The ancient Hebrew manuscript text is public domain. Hobah English prose is newly prepared for this project. Copyrighted modern critical reconstructions or translations are not copied into production wording.
translation.completeness: two-part research reading of the substantially preserved manuscript; not a diplomatic critical edition

chapters.label: Reading I — The congregation in the latter days
chapters.text: This is the rule for all the congregation of Israel in the latter days, when they assemble to walk according to the judgment of the sons of Zadok, the priests, and the men of their covenant. From youth a child shall be instructed in the book and learn the statutes of the covenant. As he grows, he is advanced according to age, knowledge, and ability. At twenty years he may enter among those numbered for the congregation and take responsibility according to the rule. Marriage, testimony, office, and service are tied to maturity and standing. The chiefs, judges, officers, priests, and Levites shall sit according to rank when the whole congregation is summoned. Certain serious bodily impairments exclude a person from particular sacred or military functions described here, though the surviving lines are damaged and the exact scope of several rules is disputed. No one shall speak before a person of higher rank without permission, and counsel shall proceed in ordered sequence so that the congregation acts with knowledge rather than confusion.

chapters.label: Reading II — Council and the messianic meal
chapters.text: When God brings forth the Messiah among them, the chief priest of all the congregation shall enter first, and with him his priestly brothers. After them the Messiah of Israel shall enter, and the chiefs of the thousands of Israel shall sit before him, each according to rank. When they gather at the common table and the wine is mixed for drinking, no one shall stretch out a hand toward the first portion of bread or wine before the priest. The priest shall bless the first portion, and afterward the Messiah of Israel shall stretch out his hands toward the bread. Then the whole congregation shall bless and eat according to rank. This order shall be followed whenever they assemble for the common meal in the time described by the rule. [The final lines are damaged.]
